chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Husayn ibn Rashid from al-Husayn ibn Aslama who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him), 'I am in the market and recognize the time, but it becomes difficult for me to enter [the market] so that I may pray.' He said, 'Satan aligns with the sun in three conditions: when it rises, when it is high (at noon), and when it sets. So pray after Zawal (decline), for Satan wants to place you on a boundary that is cut off for you without it.'
ai.seo_question: When is the best time to pray optional prayers during the day to avoid Satan's influence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the jurisprudential rationale behind avoiding the three specific times of sun alignment—rising, full height, and setting—for optional prayers, linking them to Satan's influence. It emphasizes that praying after Zawal (decline of the sun) ensures acceptance by avoiding the period where Satan seeks to cause rejection or distraction. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between times of prohibition (Karahat/Tahrim) and times of acceptance for Nafl prayers.
